name: East Asian Lang Cultures (MA)

children.name: Proseminar Sequence Requirement (EALC 201)
children.desc: Complete two proseminar courses, EALC 201 in the first year of study and an additional course as associated with the student's subplan. EALC 202 is required for all literature students, CHINA 290 is required for all Chinese linguistics students, and JAPAN 279 is required for all Japanese linguistics students. Students in Chinese archaeology must take an advisor-approved course with subject code CHINA, ARCHLGY, or ANTHRO.

children.name: Advisor-Approved Additional Courses Requirement
children.desc: Six advisor-approved courses in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and/or trans-Asian literature, culture, linguistics, anthropology, archaeology, art and art history, history, philosophy, political science, religious studies, sociology, or another field, as associated with the student's subplan or approved by the advisor, not including courses taken to fulfill the proseminar or language requirements.

Submit a full draft of the student's M.A. thesis to the primary advisor by May 15 of Spring Quarter and the final version by the last Friday of May. Students are also required to present M.A. thesis research at the last meeting of the East Asian Humanities and East Asian Linguistics workshops (the joint student symposium) at the end of Spring Quarter.

gpa: Students are expected to earn an overall GPA of 3.0 or better across all courses.
grading: Students must take all required courses for a letter grade when this option is available, and receive a grade of B+ or better in all required coursework.
reviewNotes: You choose one track in your subplan: four in East Asian Literatures (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Trans-Asian) and two in East Asian Linguistics (Chinese, Japanese). Everyone takes EALC 201, a second proseminar for the subplan (EALC 202 for literature, CHINA 290 or JAPAN 279 for linguistics, an advisor-approved CHINA, ARCHLGY or ANTHRO course for archaeology), the track's language and course requirements, and EALC 299 for the thesis. Every required course must be taken for a letter grade when one is offered and passed with a B+ or better, and the degree needs 45 units. The audit checks the subject, level and number of the advisor-approved courses; you confirm by hand your advisor's approval of them, the six advisor-approved courses, language proficiency shown by exam, the thesis and symposium presentation, and the 3.0 GPA. Chinese Archaeology students bring the total to 45 units with courses from that subplan's list; the audit checks the 45 units, not that the extra ones come from the list.
